title: Census 1951, Rajasthan and Ajmer: District Census Handbook Bikaner, Part II - Primary Census Abstract or Village Directory
villages_named: ladera (serial 54, p.25 -- a second 'Ladera' also exists in Bikaner tehsil, p.~14, so this name has a namesake)
lakhor (as 'Lakhor J36ri', OCR-garbled, serial 31, p.25 -- corresponds to Lakhor Chhoti/Moti but exact qualifier illegible)
bhanabasti (as 'Bhana Basti', p.45, List of Hamlets under Tehsil-2 Lunkaransar)
what_it_contains: THE single most valuable document found: the official pre-1982 (in fact pre-1971 and pre-1961 too) village-by-village census abstract for Lunkaransar tehsil, Bikaner district, from the 1951 Census of India. Lists every revenue village in Tehsil Lunkaransar alphabetically with a serial number, village code, Roman and Devanagari name, area, houses, households, and population by sex, literacy and livelihood class (columns 1-28 spread across several sub-tables per village, pp.16-33 for the whole district covering all 4 tehsils; Lunkaransar tehsil specifically is pp.21-29 approx. for the main directory, plus a 'List of Unpopulated Villages' and 'List of Hamlets' on pp.40-42/45 that include Bhana Basti). OCR text (Adobe Scan-to-PDF, fairly noisy on the Devanagari and on numeric-heavy table cells but usable) confirms 22 of our 37 candidate names existed as named villages/hamlets in Lunkaransar tehsil in 1951, three decades before the 1982-86 MFFR acquisition. File saved locally as dch_bikaner_1951_partII_village_directory.pdf/.txt (47pp, 1.5MB).
how_to_get: Direct download currently blocked from this machine (censusindia.gov.in refuses/SSL-fails here) but the file IS live on the official NADA portal at the URL above (catalog record https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/28566 ). A person with normal internet access should just open that URL and download the PDF. We recovered a full working copy via the Wayback Machine snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20250419033144/https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/28566/download/31748/23629_1951_BIK.pdf and saved it locally -- see files list.
evidence: '3. No. and Name of Tehsil-2. LUNKARAN8AR ... 1 154 Adsar ... 2 58 Ajitmana ... 47 Bhojrasar ... 9 Dewasar ... 22 Berawala ... 55 Bhunwa.la ... 7 Hathu"ar ... 8 Jagore ... 10 Kanolw< ... 46 Kankratia ... 36 Khanisar ... 49 Khiana ... Kumbhaaa ... 54 Ladera ... 31 Lakhor J36ri ... 38 Meusar ... 20 Motasar ... 33 Rampura ... 27 Thoiyan' (OCR text, dch_bikaner_1951_partII_village_directory.txt); hamlet list p.45: 'Tehsi1:-2 LUNKARANSAR ... Bhana Basti'

title: Census 1951, Rajasthan and Ajmer: District Census Handbook Bikaner, Part I - General Description and Census Tables
what_it_contains: Companion volume to the Part II village directory above: narrative description of Bikaner district (4 tehsils: Bikaner, Lunkaransar, Nokha, Kolayat/Magra), history, geography, and tehsil-level (not village-level) summary tables -- e.g. Lunkaransar Tehsil Total population figures. Confirms Lunkaransar tehsil had 3,135 sq. miles and lists it among the district's four tehsils repeatedly (pp.1-40ish). Useful for context/area figures but does NOT itself list individual villages by name -- that is only in Part II above. 135pp OCR text saved locally as dch_bikaner_1951_partI_general.txt (Part I PDF itself was corrupted on re-download and was not kept; the text extraction is preserved and the PDF is re-fetchable from the Wayback URL below).
how_to_get: Official URL above (catalog https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/29012 ); recoverable via Wayback: https://web.archive.org/web/20250418194239/https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/29012/download/32193/49703_1951_BIK.pdf (7.5MB, valid 135-page PDF -- re-download this if the local copy is needed again).
evidence: 'Lunkaransar TehsilTotal / Rural / Urban' (tehsil summary table); 'There are 4 tehsil's in this district namely Bikaner, Lunkaransar, Nokha and Kolayat (Magra).'

title: Census of India 2001, District Census Handbook, Bikaner

Not yet inspected.

A person should try the URL directly (https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/43862 ) or search NADA for 'Bikaner 2001 district census handbook'.

title: AMS Series U502 India & Pakistan 1:250,000, Sheet NH 43-13 "Bikaner" (US Army Map Service, ~1955)
what_it_contains: Public-domain 1:250,000 topographic sheet covering lat 28-29N, lon 72-73.5E -- i.e. the SOUTHWESTERN quarter of the MFFR bounding box (28.55-29.04N, 73.30-73.80E). Large-format scan (5000x3947px, 3.3MB) showing every named settlement, well and track circa 1955, predating the 1982-86 acquisition by ~27 years. Downloaded locally as files/ams_nh43-13_bikaner.jpg. Village labels are small and need zoom/crop to read; not yet individually transcribed.
how_to_get: Live site blocked by an Anubis bot-check from this machine (https://maps.lib.utexas.edu/maps/ams/india/index.html). title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 4236, 21 Aug 1987: Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan

title: Census 2011 mirror: Mahajan Fieldfiring Range village (code 069202), Lunkaransar, Bikaner
what_it_contains: Already identified in prior TechnoTaau research. Confirms that by 2011 the Census treats the entire acquired area as a single merged census village named 'Mahajan Fieldfiring Range' (code 69202) -- i.e. all 33/34 original villages were administratively absorbed into one unit and no longer appear individually in modern census data. Cross-mirrored at villageinfo.in, vill.co.in, mapsofindia.com, localbodydata.com (all consistent), useful for confirming which candidate names have NO living namesake elsewhere in Lunkaransar tehsil today (i.e. are unambiguously inside the range) vs. which do (namesake risk, e.g. Ladera and Kumbhasar per the 1951 census cross-check above).
how_to_get: Loads directly; no download needed.

title: Census of India NADA (National Data Archive) portal -- general catalog

The 1961, 1971 and 1981 Bikaner DCH catalog IDs were NOT located in this session (budget-limited; the site itself is unreachable from this machine for interactive browsing/searching). These are the single highest-value missing documents for this project -- the 1981 Part XIII-A Village & Town Directory in particular would show the villages exactly as they stood ~1-5 years before acquisition.

If a catalog ID is found but the site is down again, try the Wayback Machine the same way we recovered the 1951 files: https://web.archive.org/web/2025*/censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/<ID>*
